title: InfoQ Online Cohorts Address AI Security and Coding Agent Verification
gist: Promotional piece for two InfoQ five-week certification cohorts starting October 2026: AI Security & Privacy Engineering (Katharine Jarmul) and AI-Assisted Engineering (Thoughtworks' Zichuan Xiong and Premanand Chandrasekaran). Its limited signal is the framing of coding-agent work as harness engineering: context, scoped permissions, tests, separated generation and review, and CI checks.

insights.claim: Thoughtworks practitioners frame the core problem of coding agents not as speed of change but as verifying what the agent was allowed to do and whether the change is sound.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Value in AI-assisted development is shifting toward verification, permissions and guardrail tooling.
insights.quote: A coding agent can make a change quickly, but the harder question is what it was allowed to do and how we know the change is sound.

insights.claim: The recommended harness for agents working in brownfield codebases is: build context, limit permissions, add tests and sensors, separate generation from review, then move checks into CI.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Outlines the tooling stack (sandboxing, testing, review, CI) enterprises will buy around coding agents.
insights.quote: separate generation from review before moving checks into CI
insights.locator: In the InfoQ AI-Assisted Engineering Program

insights.claim: Manually reviewing every agent change does not reveal which checks should be codified into the engineering workflow, so independent review and CI checks should be measured against prior expectations.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Human review does not scale with agent output, so automated verification becomes the bottleneck to invest in.
insights.quote: Reviewing every agent change by hand does not tell us which checks should become part of the engineering workflow.

insights.claim: An AI security review should follow sensitive data and decisions across the whole system, using threat modeling and red teaming, testing chosen controls, and assigning ownership of residual risk.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Data-flow-centric AI security creates demand for governance, red-teaming and privacy tooling.
insights.quote: An AI security review has to follow the data and the decisions across the whole system.
insights.locator: Katharine Jarmul, author of Practical Data Privacy

insights.claim: InfoQ is launching paid five-week certification cohorts on AI security and AI-assisted engineering in October 2026, reflecting practitioner demand for training on governing AI systems and coding agents.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Minor indicator that agent verification and AI security are becoming formal professional skill categories.
